en.title: Sum of Maximum Times Length Over All Subarrays
en.description:
Every non-empty contiguous subarray contributes its maximum multiplied by its length; find the sum of all contributions. Negative numbers are allowed, and the answer must be output exactly, without any modulus; a linear-time algorithm is required.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains n integers. The source gives no value bounds; on this site 0≤n≤200000 and elements are in −10^9..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 59; -12; and 0, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use a monotonic stack to find, for each element, the nearest strictly greater position on its left and the nearest greater-or-equal position on its right, and let the distances to these boundaries be L and R. The element is responsible for L·R subarrays whose lengths total L·R·(L+R)/2; multiply this by the element and accumulate.
